questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn's abdominal organs protrude through the umbilicus in a translucent sac. What is the FIRST care?
questions.rationale: Omphalocele: cover the sac immediately with sterile NSS-soaked gauze to prevent drying.
questions.quote: cover sac with sterile gauze soaked in normal saline to prevent drying

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How does gastroschisis differ from omphalocele?
questions.rationale: Gastroschisis is lateral to the umbilicus with no membrane; omphalocele has a sac at the umbilicus.
questions.quote: No membranes cover the exposed bowel

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother wants to tape a coin over her baby's umbilical hernia. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Taping coins does not help; most umbilical hernias close by about age 3.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Umbilical Hernias (PDF p. 233)
questions.quote: In most cases, by age 3 the umbilical hernia shrinks and closes without treatment

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Why are clubfoot casts changed every 1–2 weeks in newborns?
questions.rationale: Rapid neonatal growth requires frequent cast changes during correction.
questions.quote: Infants grow so rapidly in the neonatal period that casts for talipes deformities must be change

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which test feels the femoral head slip out of the socket in hip dysplasia?
questions.rationale: Barlow pushes the femur out (instability); Ortolani relocates it with a 'clunk'.
questions.quote: Barlow test is the most important maneuver in examining the newborn hip

questions.subject: NP II

questions.stem: How is DDH corrected in the newborn period?
questions.rationale: Positioning hips flexed and abducted (frog-leg), such as with multiple diapers or splints, deepens the acetabulum.

questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn has fluid in the scrotum present at birth with no hernia. This is usually:
questions.rationale: Non-communicating hydrocele is trapped fluid seen at birth and needs no treatment.
